holidays.name: National Nothing Day
holidays.description: A day for doing absolutely nothing. You don't have to celebrate, honor, or observe anything. Sit back, stare at the wall, and enjoy having no obligations.
holidays.origin: Journalist and columnist Harold Pullman Coffin started it in the early 1970s. He wanted one day when people could simply sit without celebrating or honoring anything. It was later recognized in national holiday listings.
holidays.funFact: Nothing Day is a holiday about not celebrating anything, yet people celebrate it anyway by doing nothing on purpose. That makes it one of the most paradoxical days on the calendar.

holidays.name: National Fig Newton Day
holidays.description: A salute to the soft, jammy, cake-wrapped fig cookie. It has been a lunchbox staple for generations. Today is a good day to eat a few and argue about whether it's a cookie or a pastry.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It celebrates the fig-filled cookie that the Kennedy Biscuit Company of Massachusetts began making in the 1890s.
holidays.funFact: Fig Newtons are named after Newton, Massachusetts, not Sir Isaac Newton. The Kennedy Biscuit Company named many of its cookies after nearby towns.

holidays.name: International Hot & Spicy Food Day
holidays.description: A day for people who like their meals with a kick. Add the hot sauce, the jalapeños, and the ghost pepper if you dare. Your taste buds will be working hard today.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages everyone to enjoy fiery cuisines from around the world.
holidays.funFact: The burn of a chili pepper comes from capsaicin. Your brain reads it as pain and heat rather than flavor, and it can trigger a rush of endorphins.
